findings.what: Service.name is presentation copy but also the only service identity across promotions, price history, UI state, DOM IDs, React keys, and analytics.
findings.why_it_matters: A customer-facing rename can silently detach campaigns, fork regulated price history, and change UI and analytics identity. The repeated consultation name turns referential integrity into coordinated text editing.
findings.counter_argument: The finding groups two different kinds of name use and assigns the combined set a High blast radius. UI state, React keys, DOM IDs, analytics properties, and the default price-history key are derived directly from the current Service object, so a catalog rename changes them together rather than detaching them. Default history is rebuilt by mapping the current services and assigning service.name to each entry; it is not a separately keyed checked-in history table. The concrete independent reference is promotion.applicability.serviceNames, whose exact string match can stop applying after an incomplete rename. That is a real static-configuration maintainability defect, but the repository evidence supports a bounded campaign/configuration failure, not a broad High-severity identity-integrity failure.
findings.fix_direction: Add a stable service ID and use it for references, history, state, keys, DOM IDs, and analytics; keep name presentation-only and validate references.

findings.what: Default price history is regenerated from today's catalog price and campaign starts, including future and unchanged checkpoints but no explicit campaign-end transitions.
findings.why_it_matters: A price edit rewrites historical baselines and promotional prices. Current-price synchronization can compare against a future final point and append repeated present points, so the 30-day result depends on configuration, view timing, and process lifetime.
findings.counter_argument: F-002 combines a real historical-data modeling weakness with timing and process-lifetime effects whose production blast radius is overstated. The lowest-price query expressly removes future checkpoints before selecting candidates, and synchronization appends only when the latest configured value differs from the effective current price. In the checked-in July-December 2026 campaign sequence, the consultation discount is unchanged month to month; its final future value is therefore the same 300 PLN effective price used during the current campaign, while services outside the campaign retain their base price. The alleged future-point comparison consequently does not append repeatedly on the current production path. Repeated appends require an earlier or newly introduced interval whose effective current price differs from the last future checkpoint, and duplicates of the same price do not alter the minimum. High severity is therefore not supported by the full composite claim.
findings.fix_direction: Choose immutable effective-price transitions with start/end events or pure time-based derivation; do not reconstruct past facts from today's base price.

findings.what: Deferred sections have Suspense loading fallbacks but no local error containment or recovery for a rejected dynamic import.
findings.why_it_matters: A missing or transiently unavailable optional chunk can escape to route-level handling after the page has appeared instead of degrading only that section.
findings.counter_argument: The High rating overstates an uncommon, already contained availability fault. TanStack Start documents that it uses TanStack Router route-level error boundaries, and the repository does not disable that behavior. A rejected deferred import therefore reaches a router error boundary and built-in error UI rather than becoming an uncaught application or server failure. The ordinary initial response also server-renders and eagerly hydrates the salon's hero, about, process, quote, and full services catalog before any deferred import is mounted. Triggering the finding requires a fingerprinted chunk to be unavailable or fail evaluation; repository deployment guidance calls for aggressive caching of fingerprinted assets and uncached or short-TTL SSR HTML, which reduces deployment skew. These controls do not make the issue false, but they make High disproportionate for a single-route brochure site with no transactional or data-loss consequence.
findings.fix_direction: Contain deferred sections with an appropriate local error boundary and bounded recovery behavior where evidence shows route-level handling is insufficient.

findings.what: A service-card render mutates the exported module-level price-history array from inside useMemo.
findings.why_it_matters: A read-looking render owns a process-wide state transition with no request, component, or persistence boundary. React retries and long-lived SSR processes make behavior depend on render count and process lifetime.
findings.counter_argument: Writes are usually deterministic public data and equality checks avoid some duplicate updates.
findings.fix_direction: Keep render-time price derivation pure and move real history changes to an explicit immutable lifecycle or persistence owner.

findings.what: The data API models multiple active campaigns, but service UI behavior selects the first while history evaluates all; overlap policy is undefined.
findings.why_it_matters: An overlapping campaign makes array order an implicit pricing and visibility rule, and different consumers can resolve a different effective offer.
findings.counter_argument: Current campaigns do not overlap, so singular selection may be an undocumented product invariant.
findings.fix_direction: Validate that overlap is forbidden or define deterministic service-level precedence in one resolver used by UI and history.

findings.what: Malformed static campaign dates are silently skipped and the suite has no whole-configuration integrity gate for dates, IDs, ranges, or catalog references.
findings.why_it_matters: A typo can become the normal no-promotion UI while builds, historical mechanism tests, and the generic homepage health check remain green.
findings.counter_argument: Fail-open behavior preserves site availability when one historical record is malformed.
findings.fix_direction: Validate the complete production campaign set at build/test time while allowing runtime selection to operate on already validated input.

findings.what: Salon/location facts have separate canonical-looking owners in contact data, route JSON-LD, presentation components, map URL, and public metadata.
findings.why_it_matters: A move or channel change can leave customer-visible content, maps, structured search data, and public metadata inconsistent. The measured second-location trace touches 14 production, 14 test, and 3 documentation files.
findings.counter_argument: SEO-specific representation legitimately belongs at the route boundary and the business is currently a single location.
findings.fix_direction: Own typed brand/location facts once and derive route, UI, map, and public representations through explicit adapters.

findings.what: The full-suite script is named ci while maintainer docs prescribe pnpm ci, which pnpm 11.11.0 resolves to its built-in clean install rather than this script.
findings.why_it_matters: The documented substantial-PR command can remove dependencies and exit without running repository quality gates; this was reproduced during preconditions.
findings.counter_argument: GitHub Actions runs stages directly and experienced pnpm users may know to include run.
findings.fix_direction: Use a non-conflicting aggregate script name or consistently document pnpm run ci across all authoritative surfaces.

findings.what: Promotion E2E tests freeze only the browser clock while SSR uses the host clock; the promotion path failed once on Mobile Safari and passed unchanged on rerun.
findings.why_it_matters: Initial SSR and hydrated promotion states can differ, and the page object does not wait on a stable promotion-ready contract. The full suite is empirically flaky in the exact time-sensitive flow.
findings.counter_argument: The second run passed and no retained trace proves the split clock caused the timeout.
findings.fix_direction: Inject one test reference time into SSR and browser behavior and synchronize on a user-visible ready state; retain evidence for recovered flakes.

findings.quote:
## Dokploy

Configure the application as a Node service:

- Install: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- Build: `pnpm build`
- Start: `pnpm start`
- Port: set `PORT` to the port exposed through Dokploy
- Health check: `/`

The Nitro build is written to `.output/`. Cloudflare may cache fingerprinted
assets aggressively; SSR HTML should remain uncached or use a short TTL.
findings.what: Operations documentation ends at build/start and a generic homepage check, with no release identity, content verification, rollback/cache procedure, owner, or external runbook pointer.
findings.why_it_matters: A stale or missing promotion can coexist with a healthy root response. A repository-only responder cannot identify the deployed revision, execute rollback/cache recovery, or escalate through a documented owner.
findings.counter_argument: Dokploy, Cloudflare, or organization-level runbooks may provide these capabilities externally.
findings.fix_direction: Provide a canonical runbook or pointer covering release identity, expected-content verification, rollback, cache invalidation, and escalation ownership.

findings.what: Analytics initialization converts import failure to null, retains the failed promise, and emits no independent diagnostic.
findings.why_it_matters: A transient failure disables retry for the page session and removes telemetry precisely during client asset or network incidents.
findings.counter_argument: Analytics is deliberately non-critical and retrying can add main-thread/network work or duplicate initialization.
findings.fix_direction: Define bounded retry or explicit non-retry policy and an independent minimal diagnostic appropriate to a non-critical analytics path.

findings.what: ServiceCategory conflates catalog taxonomy with Vouchery and Promocje section view modes, although no service uses those pseudo-categories.
findings.why_it_matters: The Service model permits values that require special rendering, and adding a real category versus a new section mode follows one misleading convention.
findings.counter_argument: The union maps directly to six visible buttons and keeps a small section simple.
findings.fix_direction: Separate service taxonomy from a discriminated section filter/view-mode type.

findings.what: OpeningHours is an unrestricted string dictionary whose example key language disagrees with production data and cannot validate weekdays, closed days, intervals, or timezone.
findings.why_it_matters: Misspelled or malformed schedules compile, while UI and JSON-LD need different representations and are already maintained separately.
findings.counter_argument: The current formatter and single location keep the flexible dictionary easy to edit.
findings.fix_direction: Use explicit weekdays, structured open/closed slots, and timezone, then derive UI and Schema.org formats.

findings.what: CI can recover after two E2E retries, while retry traces are uploaded only if the overall job ultimately fails.
findings.why_it_matters: A recovered Mobile Safari instability can turn the gate green without preserving the evidence needed to characterize it.
findings.counter_argument: Retries are standard browser-noise mitigation and the GitHub reporter can annotate flaky tests.
findings.fix_direction: Define an explicit flake policy and retain retry evidence for recovered flaky tests until characterized.

findings.what: Twelve monthly records repeat one campaign's service reference, discount, price copy, and CTA while only calendar fields change.
findings.why_it_matters: Extending or changing the campaign requires synchronized edits across a literal schedule, and copied prices can disagree with catalog-derived discounted prices.
findings.counter_argument: Explicit monthly records are easy to inspect and allow future month-specific exceptions.
findings.fix_direction: Represent recurrence once while preserving generated month-level IDs if needed, and derive price presentation from catalog and discount data.
